home.heroLede: A Vietnamese American parade krewe for Greater Sacramento
home.definition: A coordinated Vietnamese American parade presence for Greater Sacramento — groups marching together as a krewe. From past parade efforts, we grow toward a prestigious parade corps.
home.kreweBody: In New Orleans Mardi Gras tradition, a krewe is a social club that organizes to parade together — shared identity, costumes, and presence on the route. We borrow that idea: Vietnamese American groups showing up as a coordinated train at civic parades across Greater Sacramento.

chapters.headline: A parade we used to host
chapters.body: In 2010, neighbors marched Tết down Stockton Blvd on Little Saigon’s designation weekend. Two years later the community hosted a branded Little Saigon Tết parade weekend — a community parade, not a krewe. Elk Grove Lunar New Year 2026 tried that host spirit again. What it showed was how thin Vietnamese participation in parading had become. Little Saigon Krewe is how we start rebuilding a train.

chapters.headline: A professionally run parade corps
chapters.body: Imagine winning awards. Getting recognition. Inspiring every generation to come. That is the krewe we are building — not a one-off photo line, a corps that shows up again and again.
chapters.imageAlt: Language school banner and pageant sashes in the Elk Grove Lunar New Year parade

chapters.headline: Arts, craft, and standing with our roots
chapters.body: This only happens when we pour our hearts into our arts and crafts, come together to support each other, and stand tall with feet planted firmly with our roots.
chapters.imageAlt: Fan dancers marching in the parade

chapters.headline: Golden Harvest — Saturday, October 24, 2026
chapters.body: Little Saigon Krewe begins that journey at the Golden Harvest Parade on Capitol Mall. Check-in around 9:00. March at 11:00. Group officers: timelines, registration, and waivers live on the Golden Harvest page.

host-2010.headline: Little Saigon designation — and a New Year parade
host-2010.body: City and County ribbon cuttings, and a Tết parade down Stockton Blvd toward Florin. Neighbors filled the corridor that designation weekend — we marched in Little Saigon.

host-2012.headline: Little Saigon Street Festival Parade
host-2012.body: The corridor filled again — GSVACC, Florin Partnership, and many amateur cameras. Rain moved the weekend from January 21 to this Saturday. LITTLE SAIGON TV taped it; it remains the best-recorded Little Saigon Tết parade we have.

host-2013.headline: Xuân Quý Tỵ Parade
host-2013.body: A corridor parade and hội chợ on Stockton Blvd / Florin after the branded weekend. HyRo taped the street parade that Saturday.

host-2014.headline: Giáp Ngọ Parade
host-2014.body: VACOS hosted parade and hội chợ at NE Florin & Stockton Blvd (rain-moved). SBTN taped both the march and the lot.
host-2014.youtubeTitle: Diễn hành và Hội Chợ Tết Giáp Ngọ 2014 (SBTN)

host-2016.headline: Little Saigon Tet Parade + Lunar Flower Festival
host-2016.body: Parade at 9 AM, Stockton Blvd & Fruitridge — the same Saturday as the lot festival. HeuFamilyEnt taped the march; KCRA named both hosts.
host-2016.youtubeTitle: Little Saigon Lunar Flower Fest 2016 — Parade (HeuFamilyEnt)

host-2017.headline: Đinh Dậu Parade
host-2017.body: The street march landed on Tết Saturday, from the Happy Garden lot along Stockton Blvd into the hội chợ. SN&R also billed a Florin & Stockton Blvd fair Saturday–Sunday, February 4–5 — a later weekend, not this tape.

host-2024.headline: Civic Tết at Elk Grove Park
host-2024.body: Civic Tết moves to Elk Grove Park on the Lunar New Year weekend. Nhịp Sống Cali taped the park parade.

march-ghp.headline: cPALSs, NVCC, pageant — on Capitol Mall
march-ghp.body: Golden Harvest Parade & Festival is at Capitol Mall, and has been running since 2022. Vietnamese entries already walk it: cPALSs / NVCC and Mrs. Vietnam (2022–23), Mrs. Vietnam and Xang Xu Liu (2024), then a thicker 2025 line (Viet Serenity Sisters, pageant, cPALSs, NVCC). Little Saigon Krewe’s first stop is the 2026 edition — as a train, not as the host.

march-scouts-vets.body: Pack and Troop 243 already know how to be a unit on a civic street: uniforms, US and heritage flags, rows of youth. Their Veterans Day 2025 appearance is that grammar — precedent for a krewe train, not a community-hosted Tết parade.

pitch.headline: Check in around 9:00. March as a train.
pitch.body: On Golden Harvest morning you’ll check in around 9:00, line up with peers who share your world — high school with high school, college with college — and march at 11:00 as a train of krewe groups, one after another. We are your front door to Golden Harvest: one place for questions. Each group still registers under its own name.

portal.headline: Participant waivers
portal.body: Every marcher needs a participant waiver — adults consent for themselves; parents or guardians consent for minors. Officers sign in, register the club, and share the join link. This is the cPALSs gate, separate from Golden Harvest’s own participant forms.
portal.cutoff: Participant waivers due Saturday, October 17, 2026 — one week before the parade. No night-before or day-of paperwork.

timeline.intro: Stay with Little Saigon Krewe for questions — we’ll batch anything Golden Harvest needs so your club doesn’t have to chase two organizations. Soft interest first; paperwork comes in later gates.

faq.q: Should I register through the Golden Harvest site?
faq.a: No — register through Little Saigon Krewe first. Clubs can register with Golden Harvest on their own. Golden Harvest is looking for at least 15 members per group. Our job is to combine smaller groups so the combined headcount meets that minimum.

No. Groups arrange their own ride — drive, carpool, or take SacRT on their own. Little Saigon Krewe is not running a bus or a staffed light-rail escort. The 2025 parade packet had a SacRT free-ride coupon (not a krewe shuttle); look for whether 2026 repeats that.

faq.q: Do we perform along the whole route?
faq.aHtml: No. Golden Harvest says parade teams may perform briefly — about 2–3 minutes — in front of the main stage and a second small stage. The rest of Capitol Mall is a walking march. Detailed route information comes about two weeks before the parade.

faq.a: No. Golden Harvest does not provide changing rooms. Plan to arrive dress-ready. There is space on Capitol Mall for practice and warm-up before step-off.

Not currently — no required uniform. The parade is televised, though, so dress in a way that shows your club or group identity (colors, shirts, banners, traditional wear if you like). Costume OK; traditional optional.

transit.headline: Getting there
transit.intro: This year families drive, carpool, or take transit on their own. Little Saigon Krewe is not running a chartered bus or a staffed light-rail escort.

steps: Take a SacRT Elk Grove local bus toward Cosumnes River College (CRC) — the southern end of the Blue Line.
Board Blue Line light rail toward Watt / I-80 (downtown direction).
Exit at 8th & Capitol Station. Walk one block east to 9th St — check-in and marching line-up are on 9th at Capitol Mall.
Return: board Blue Line at 8th & Capitol toward Cosumnes River College (check the headsign), then Elk Grove bus home.
notes: Saturday schedules differ from weekday rush-hour — Elk Grove weekday-only commuter buses (e.g. E13) won’t help parade morning. Use local EG routes + Blue Line, and verify times the week before.
Light rail uses one-way streets downtown; your outbound stop and return stop may differ.
Florin / South Sacramento riders can often skip the Elk Grove bus leg and board Blue Line closer to home.

champions.headline: Meet & Greet
champions.body: We’re rallying different organizations and clubs into tribes — high school with high school, college with college, and so on — so peers meet peers before we march. Each tribe has a champion who helps facilitate those connections: they hold the tribe sign and open the conversation.

gh.joiningIntro: Interest first — we’ll switch the tag to confirmed when a group is locked.

A.name: High school
A.peers: High school clubs — VSAs and culture clubs; interclub bonding with a light cross-chapter mix
A.championProfile: Someone vested in high school clubs (e.g. a campus VSA outreach lead)

B.name: College
B.peers: Campus clubs, e.g. VSAs and VN CARES chapters
B.championProfile: A campus club officer (VSA or VN CARES) who already convenes peers

C.name: Performance
C.peers: Lion, dance, and troupe warm-up · spacing · music cues
C.championProfile: An active dancer or lion lead who needs coordination anyway

D.name: Business
D.peers: Chambers and merchants — meet peers on foot in the marching block
D.championProfile: A merchant or chamber face who wants peers to meet each other

E.name: Family & heritage
E.peers: Language school, scouts, pageant, veterans, elders
E.championProfile: Someone already in the language / scout / pageant / elder orbit

F.name: Service
F.championProfile: A peer nonprofit lead (when two or more service orgs show)

G.name: Floats & vehicles
G.peers: Anyone bringing a float, trailer, car, or pickup — stages on the vehicle block, separate from the marching line-up.
G.championProfile: Someone bringing a vehicle entry, or comfortable running the vehicle line-up

fund.headline: Fund the Krewe
fund.body: Cover breakfast, gas, water, or a banner so students and clubs can march. Cash check to cPALSs (memo LSK 2026) or in-kind that matches the gift. Ask which slots are still open before you commit.

food-15.detail: Breakfast for one student group of about 15. Groups arrive around 9:00 AM and finish by noon. Benefit: social media story — “Student breakfast presented by [You].”

college-gas-parking.need: Gas and parking for a college club
college-gas-parking.detail: Gas and parking reimbursements for one college club of about 15. Benefit: social media story — “Student club travel presented by [You].”

staging-hub.detail: Water, group signs, and name tags for the morning check-in hub. Benefit: social media story and a sponsor card on the check-in table — “Refreshments presented by [You].”

krewe-banner.detail: Krewe banner: Little Saigon Krewe / Vietnamese Americans Celebrating Greater Sacramento. Benefit: social media story and a dedicated banner saying “Thank you [Your logo/name]” carried behind the krewe banner.

presenting.detail: Champion of the community. Benefit: social media story and a dedicated banner saying “Presenting sponsor [Your logo/name]” carried behind the krewe banner.
